html:
Honiara, on the north coast of Guadalcanal, became the capital of the Solomon Islands in 1952, replacing Tulagi. It grew from the base the Americans built during the Guadalcanal campaign.

The town drew migrants from across the islands, most of all from crowded Malaita. Tension over land between Guadalcanal people and Malaitan settlers grew into the violence that led to the regional intervention of 2003.

Riots in 2006 and 2021 burned parts of Chinatown. It is the seat of the parliament of the state that Peter Kenilorea led to independence. See also Maasina Rule.
sum: Honiara, on the north coast of Guadalcanal, became the capital of the Solomon Islands in 1952, replacing Tulagi. It grew from the base the Americans built during the Guadalcanal campaign.
